entries.def:
μνήμη, -ης, ἡ
(μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן ;] 
memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive, to remember, 2Pe.1.15 (but in cl., π., μ. π. more frequently = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l; and for ex. from π., see Zorell, see word).†
SYN.: μνεία, q.v (AS)

μνημονεύω
(μνήμων, mindful) [in LXX for זָכַר ;] 
__1. to call to mind, remember : absol., Mrk.8.18 with genitive of person(s), Luk.17.32, Col.4.18, 1Th.1.3, Heb.11.15 (but see infr.) Heb.13.7 τ. πτωχῶν, Gal.2.20 with genitive of thing(s), Jhn.15.20; 16.4, 21, Act.20.35; with accusative obj. (as more frequently in cl.), of persons, 2Ti.2.8 of things, Mat.16.9, 1Th.2.9, Rev.18.5; before ὅτι, Act.20.31, Eph.2.11,…

μνημόσυνον, -ου, τό
(μνήμων, mindful), [in LXX frequently for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
a memorial: Mat.26.13, Mrk.14.9, Act.10.4 (where cf. Lev.2.9, 16; 5.12, Num_5:28, Sir.45.16, al.).†
(AS)

μνηστεύω 
[in LXX for אָרַשׂ pi., pu. ;] 
__1. to woo and win, espouse. 
__2. to promise in marriage, betroth; pass., of the woman, to be be­trothed: with dative of person(s), Mat.1.18, Luk.1.27; 2.5.†
(AS)

μογι-λάλος, -ον
(μόγις, λάλος), [in LXX: Isa.35.6 (אִלֵּם) * ;] 
speaking with difficulty: Mrk.7.32 (Tr., txt., μογγιλάλος, thick-voiced, see Swete, in l).†
(AS)

μόγις
adv. (μόγος, toil), [in LXX: Wis.9.16 א A (μόγις, B), 3Ma.7.6 * ;] 
with toil or difficulty, hardly: Luk.9.39 (μόγις, WH).†
(AS)

μοιχαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(= Att.. μοιχάς, fem. of μοιχός), [in LXX: Pro.18.22 30:20), Ezk.16.38; 23.45, Hos.3.1, Mal.3.5 (נַאֲפוּף, נָאַף) * ;] 
an adulteress: Rom.7.3 meton., for μοιχεία, 2Pe.2.14. Metaphorical, of infidelity to God (cf. Ezk.16.15 ff. Ezk.23.43 ff., al.), Jas.4.4; as an adj., Mat.12.39; 16.4, Mrk.8.8.†
(AS)

ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς, 
of person(s) pron. 
I. 
__(a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in Mat.3.11, Mrk.1.8, Luk.3.16, al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as Mat.10.16, Jhn.10.17; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. 1Ki.3.8), Act.9.10; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, Jhn.1.23 (LXX), Act.7.32 (LXX). 
__(b) The enclitic forms (see…

1. an adulteress , (New Testament):as adjective adulterous , (New Testament) 
2. as Substantive = μοιχεία, (New Testament) (ML)

μοιχάω, -ῶ 
(= cl. μοιχεύω), [in LXX (mid., absol. and with accusative, with party of either sex as subj.) : Jer.3.8; 5.7; 7.9; 9.2; 23.14; 29.23, Ezk.16.32; 23.37, 43 (נָאַף) * ;] 
to commit adultery with: with accusative, fem. In NT always mid, in same sense; of the man : absol., Mat.5.32; 19.9 (WH, txt., R, mg., om.); before ἐπ᾽ αὐτήν, Mrk.10.11 of the woman: Mrk.10.12.†
(AS)
